title: NASA Marshall Crews Move Artemis III SLS Adapter for Next Phase of Manufacturing
description: These photos and videos show move crews at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, transporting the launch vehicle stage adapter (LVSA) for NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket to another facility for the next phase of manufacturing. At the new facility, technicians will begin preparing for frangible joint assembly on the flight hardware that will be used for Artemis III, which will land astronauts on the Moon to advance long-term lunar exploration and scientific discovery and inspire the Artemis Generation. The frangible joint assembly, located at the top of the adapter, separates the LVSA and the rocket’s core stage, located below the LVSA, from the upper elements of the SLS rocket and the Orion spacecraft.  The LVSA is fully manufactured at Marshall by NASA, lead contractor Teledyne Brown Engineering, and the Jacobs Space Group’s ESSCA contract. The LVSA for Artemis III is the last of its kind as future SLS rockets will transition to its next, more powerful Block 1B configuration beginning with Artemis IV. NASA is working to land the first woman and first person of color on the Moon under Artemis. SLS is part of NASA’s backbone for deep space exploration, along with the Orion spacecraft, advanced spacesuits and rovers, the Gateway in orbit around the Moon, and commercial human landing systems. SLS is the only rocket that can send Orion, astronauts, and supplies to the Moon in a single mission.
